Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q4 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, operator assistance instructions are available by pressing star then one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q4 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Thornton, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Chen, Head of Distribution; David Patel, Head of Operations; and Sophia Grant, Head of Risk Management.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q4 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust organic inflows, market appreciation across key asset classes, and continued alpha generation in our active strategies. Our AUM grew to a record $1.92 trillion.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q4 2024. Our revenue was $2.5 billion, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM and resilient fee rates across our diversified platform. Our expenses were $1.5 billion, resulting in net income of $1.0 billion. Our expense ratio improved to 22 basis points due to operational scale, technology efficiencies, and disciplined cost management.

Let me expand on the core revenue drivers, starting with management fees, which accounted for about 78% of total fee revenue, highlighting the stability of our franchise. Management fee revenue reached $1.42 billion in the quarter, up 9% year-over-year and 3% sequentially. This reflected a 12% rise in average daily AUM to $1.85 trillion, tempered by a modest 3 basis point dip in our blended average fee rate to 77 basis points from 80 a year earlier—our 11th straight quarter of YoY growth.

Ending AUM hit $1.92 trillion, up 14% YoY, thanks to $28 billion in organic net inflows—our best Q2 since 2021—with $15 billion from retail into active equities and $13 billion from institutions in multi-asset credit and infrastructure. Market gains added $45 billion, riding the S&P 500's 8% advance and European equity rebound.

By asset class, equities fueled 55% of growth, with average equity AUM at $950 billion, up 15%, led by our flagship Global Equity Partners fund outperforming by 250 basis points over three years net. Fixed income AUM climbed 10% to $520 billion on short-duration and ESG bond flows amid the Fed's pause. Alternatives, at 18% of AUM or $345 billion, surged 20% YoY, with $8 billion in private credit inflows yielding 9-11% net amid high rates.

Regionally, North America grew 11% to 62% of AUM via RIA SMAs now at 25% of retail; EMEA expanded 16% to $420 billion on €12 billion institutional wins, including a €5 billion shift from Vanguard passives to our active ETFs; APAC shone with 22% growth to $280 billion from sovereign funds in Singapore and Japan.

On fee trends, the 77 bps blend shows mix shifts: ETFs at $320 billion or 17% of AUM averaged 22 basis points, grabbing $10 billion flows; alternatives held at 125 basis points with performance tiers unlocking upside; institutional SMAs at 55 basis points. We countered compression via new active ETFs like our Climate Transition ETF gathering $4 billion at 28 basis points, fee optimization tech for 5 basis point SMA uplifts, and custodian rebates preserving 52% net margins.

We project 8-10% management fee growth for FY25 with average AUM at $1.9-$2.0 trillion and fees stabilizing at 76-78 basis points, bolstered by alternatives targeting 25% of AUM.

Turning to AUM details more granularly, quarter-end AUM was $1.92 trillion, up 22% YoY from $1.58 trillion and 6.2% QoQ from $1.81 trillion—beating peers like BlackRock in the mid-teens. YoY mix: 45% markets, 35% organic flows, rest performance and FX. QoQ: 55% markets, 2.8 points net inflows.

Asset class breakdown: Equities at $864 billion, 45%, up 28% YoY and 8.1% QoQ, powered by S&P 500's AI surge—Nvidia et al.—with $18 billion inflows to active growth like Pinnacle Global Equity up 320 bps net, and $4.2 billion to AI Innovators ETF. Fixed income $576 billion, 30%, +15% YoY/+4.2% QoQ, $12 billion inflows to core bond adding $3.5 billion via BBB credits; Europe 40% of flows post-ECB cuts. Alternatives $384 billion, 20%, fastest at +25% YoY/+6.5% QoQ, $22 billion PE/credit mandates including $5 billion Canadian pension infra, $8 billion hedge multi-strat at 12% net, real assets +18% ESG. Cash/MMFs $96 billion, 5%, +8% YoY on 5% yields.

Regions: North America 62%, EMEA 22% +30% YoY, APAC 12% surging on Singapore hub.

This validates our Diversified Alpha push: 10 ETF conversions capturing $50 billion passives with active overlays, Aligned Wealth platform boosting retention 15% and cross-sell 28%.

Performance fees added $248 million FY24, +42% YoY, strongest since 2021. Q4 $92 million, up 28% sequential. Equities 58% or $144 million, fixed 22% $54 million, alts 20% $50 million—14% of total fees.

Equity: U.S. Large Cap Growth 32.4% net vs S&P 500 +25.6%, +680 bps, AI overweight; Sharpe 1.85 vs 1.42. Global ex-US 18.7% vs MSCI ACWI ex-USA +15.8%, +290 bps; EM 9.2% vs MSCI EM +10.6%, clawed back Q4. Fixed: Core Bond 4.8% vs Agg +3.68%, +112 bps barbell; Active Duration 5.9% +213 bps. Munis 4.2% +78 bps. Quant lab 25% equity alpha, ESG filters, private credit 11.8% IRR $32 million promote.

Supercharged $18 billion inflows, 98% retention. Expect $300-350 million FY25.

Operating expenses totaled $428 million Q4, +4.2% YoY but flat QoQ; TTM $1.71 billion +3.8%. Op ex ratio 11.9 bps avg AUM vs 12.6 bps YoY, margin 42%, adj op income $312 million +8%.

Breakdown: Comp/benefits $218 million (51%), +5.1%, headcount +2% offset variable cuts; NA 65%, EMEA +8%, APAC +12%. Tech/data $62 million (14%), +12%, AWS migration, AI Pinnacle Alpha automating 40% rebalancing, cyber $8 million. G&A $58 million (14%), +2%, legal/compliance $23 million SEC/MiFID. Distribution/marketing $52 million (12%), +1%, digital ESG campaigns. Amort/other $38 million (9%), -8%.

YTD +4% vs 11% revenue, Project Horizon $50 million savings offshore India. Guide FY25 $1.75-1.80 billion, 11.5-12 bps.

Capital allocation prioritizes ROIC, fee earnings growth, $2.8 billion net cash. Shareholder returns: 85-90% FCF, Q3 $450 million buybacks at $78/share 2.1% float, YTD $1.2 billion; dividend $0.42/share 2.2% yield. Next 12 months $1.5-2.0 billion buybacks, 50-60% payout.

Organic: 20-25% capex $800 million annual—distribution +15% team $25 billion mandates, APAC 18% AUM China ETF $18 billion, Europe Luxembourg onshore. Tech $350 million AlphaForge AI allocation, blockchain custody.

M&A: $1.1 billion Horizon Alternatives $45 billion AUM +$0.15 EPS 2025, alts 22%; pipeline $3 billion.

ROIC 18% TTM >12% WACC, EPS 10-12% growth.

Michael Thornton: Thank you, Elena. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging our quant alpha lab with machine learning on alternative data, ESG integration via Sustainability Scorecard, and tactical positioning in AI, quality growth, and credit selection. We launched an AI-thematic equity fund this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $5 billion seeded from anchor RIAs already.

Our core long-only equity funds median 15.8% TTM net vs peer 13.2% Lipper and benchmark 14.1%; YTD +9.4% vs +7.9%/+8.6%. 3/5-year first quartile 85% funds, median alpha 2.1%.

U.S. Large Cap Growth 22.3% vs S&P 500 20.1%/peers 19.7%, Nvidia/Lilly overweight. SMID Value +11.5% vs Russell 2000V 9.8%/10.2%, industrials/financials. International 12.7% vs MSCI EAFE 11.4%/10.9%, Japan cyclicals. EM +8.2% vs 7.9%/8.5%, China underweight.

Fixed Core Bond 4.2% vs Agg 2.8%/3.5%, IG corporates. HY 9.1% vs 8.3%/8.7%. Balanced 10.6% vs 9.2%. PE 18.2% IRR top decile.

Sharpe 1.12 vs 0.98 peer, IR 0.65, drawdown -11.4% vs -18.2%. U.S. +16.2%, Europe +13.1%, Asia xJP +10.4%, EM +7.8%.

Positioning: Alpha Engine 2.0 70% AUM, ESG green bonds #1, active ETFs <30 bps TER.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our alternatives funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by 22% AUM growth to $280 billion, $6 billion organic from sovereign wealth funds leveraging yen weakness and localized thematics like Asia-Pacific Renewables Infrastructure.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk, with full rollout of AI Optimizer covering 80% equity AUM by Q3, cutting trading costs 15%; RPA for real-time reconciliation saving $50 million annually; $40 million cyber zero-trust for 99.99% uptime. We're also focused on cloud migrations and gen AI for client reporting.

Sophia Grant: Thank you, David. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and geopolitical risks and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes stress-testing for 100 bps rate hikes or 20% drawdowns, maintaining 24 months liquidity plus $5 billion dry powder, and beta discipline at 0.95.

Johnathan Hale: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead.

Thank you, Elena, for that comprehensive overview of our Q4 results. Before we open the line for questions, I'd like to outline our key priorities and strategic initiatives for 2025. We closed the year with record AUM of $1.92 trillion, up 14% YoY on $85 billion net inflows—strongest since 2021. Amid moderating Fed cuts, services inflation, Middle East and U.S.-China tensions, we're focused on client alpha, resilience, compounded growth.

Four pillars: client-centric growth, product innovation/alts expansion, tech efficiency, global diversification/ESG.

Client growth: Deepen RIAs, HNWIs, SWFs; target $120 billion organic inflows, 10-12% AUM ex-markets. Expand SMAs $250 billion +22% YoY with direct indexing 50-100 bps tax-alpha for top 500 RIAs. Institutional sales for Middle East SWFs, $15 billion Abu Dhabi win, expect $20-30 billion as oil volatility shifts to U.S. alts. Retention 97%, NPS >75 via Apex Insights.

Product: Alts 28% AUM to 35% by 2027. Q1 three active ETFs: AI equity $5 billion seed, private credit interval 9-11% yields vs Ares/Blackstone, volatility hedge ETF. Evergreen privates to $150 billion: $10 billion data center RE cap rates 5%, $7 billion direct lending LIBOR+550 hedged. $2 billion tokenization pilot blockchain fractional privates, unlocking $10 trillion.

Fees steady 45 bps, ROA to 8%.

Tech: OpEx to 20 bps, $250 million next-gen platform like Aladdin $25 trillion. Apex AI Optimizer 250 bps excess, 80% equity Q3, -15% trading. RPA T+2 to real-time $50 million save. Cyber $40 million zero-trust post-CrowdStrike.

Global: U.S. 65%, APAC +25% $120 billion; Singapore hub $30 billion family offices India/SE Asia 7% GDP. LatAm $10 billion Brazil sust infra 12%. ESG 45% SFDR 8/9, net-zero 2040, $15 billion Climate ETF MSCI 4% carbon reduction, €2 trillion flows.

Outperform T. Rowe/Invesco, EPS 12-15%, dividend $2.10, ROE >18%. Disciplined execution for value.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind your AUM growth this quarter?

Johnathan Hale: Thanks, John. As Elena detailed, the 14% YoY and 6.2% QoQ growth to $1.92 trillion was balanced: strong organics at $28 billion, market tailwinds especially equities +28% YoY, and strategic flows into alts +25%. Our diversified platform across classes and regions, with APAC leading, keeps us ahead.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on your average fee rate trends amid compression?

Elena Vasquez: Absolutely, John. Blended at 77 bps reflects industry dynamics but our mix management—alts firm at 125 bps, institutional SMAs 55 bps offsetting ETF 22 bps—plus innovations like dynamic pricing via eFront partnership yielding 5 bps uplift. We expect stabilization as alts grow.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Morningstar.

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of your flagship equity funds?

Michael Thornton: Thanks, Sarah. Our U.S. Large Cap Growth returned 22.3% TTM net, beating S&P 500 by 220 bps and peers by 260 bps on AI quality; SMID Value +11.5% topping Russell by 170 bps. International strong, with tight tracking error and top-quartile risk-adjusted metrics.

Sarah Jenkins: And how is the new AI-thematic product performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Chen: Great question, Sarah. Early inflows hit $5 billion from RIAs, exceeding targets on AI infrastructure demand. Reception positive, with AUM ramping fast via Schwab/Fidelity platforms, aligning with our active ETF push.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with JPMorgan.

Mike Rivera: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

David Patel: Thanks, Mike. Tech investments like AI Optimizer and RPA delivered 15% trading cost cuts, real-time ops, $50 million savings, mirroring State Street efficiencies. Cloud and cyber uptime 99.99%, scaling with $1.92 trillion AUM.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Grant with Barclays.

Emily Grant: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Sophia Grant: Emily, our framework is robust—enhanced monitoring for vol/geopolitics, stress-tested liquidity 24+ months, low beta 0.95. Regs like SEC crypto, MiFID unbundling, SFDR are opportunities; we're compliant UCITS/ESG, turning them into competitive edges like tokenized assets.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
